title: KMS observability: metrics/tracing for latency, error codes, cache, circuit breaker, and per-tenant impact
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: KMS hardening + rotation
description:
Goal
Add production-grade observability for KMS dependencies across Hosted/Dedicated/Private to (a) catch brownouts early, (b) quantify impact/blast radius per tenant, and (c) support game days and runbooks.

Scope (this issue)
1) Metrics
- KMS call latency and result codes by provider + operation:
  - kms.encrypt, kms.decrypt, kms.generate_data_key (if applicable per provider)
  - tags: provider (aws|gcp|azure), deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private), service (control-plane|data-plane), operation, region, key_alias (sanitized), tenant_tier (if available)
- Error codes: timeout, throttling, access_denied/permission_denied, key_disabled, not_found, invalid_ciphertext, internal, unknown
- Cache metrics:
  - dek_cache_hit_total / dek_cache_miss_total
  - kek_metadata_cache_hit_total / miss_total (control plane)
  - cache_entry_age_seconds histogram (sampled)
- Circuit breaker metrics (from ENG-4226 implementation):
  - breaker_state (closed|open|half_open) gauge by provider/region
  - breaker_open_total counter with reason (consecutive_failures|timeout_rate|throttle_rate)
  - requests_rejected_total (short-circuited)
- Retry/backoff visibility:
  - kms_retries_total counter by reason
  - kms_backoff_seconds histogram (sampled)
- Per-tenant impact summaries:
  - tenant_kms_decrypt_failure_rate (rolling, computed in metrics pipeline) tagged by tenant_id_hash
  - tenant_kms_error_budget_burn (SLO-aligned) for staging/canary at minimum; production gating behind admin-only access

2) Tracing
- Ensure KMS spans are emitted with stable names and minimal high-cardinality attributes.
  - Span names: KMS.encrypt, KMS.decrypt, KMS.generateDataKey
  - Required span attributes: provider, operation, region, breaker_state, cache_hit (true|false), attempt (1..N)
  - Do NOT include raw key IDs, ciphertext, tenant IDs, or request payloads.
- Propagate trace context through the data-plane encrypt/decrypt path so SRE can tie application error spikes to KMS dependency behavior.

3) Dashboards + alerts
- Dashboards
  - Global KMS health: p50/p95/p99 latency by provider/region + error rate by code
  - Circuit breaker state overview (open breakers by region/provider)
  - Cache effectiveness (hit rate over time) with overlay of KMS latency (to validate cache TTL mitigations)
  - Tenant impact summary (top N tenants by decrypt failures; admin-only)
- Alerts (initial proposal; tune post-game day)
  - Page: sustained decrypt error rate > 0.5% for 10m in any region/provider (production)
  - Page: breaker open > 5m impacting decrypt path for any production cluster
  - Ticket: throttle rate increase > 3x baseline for 30m
  - Ticket: cache hit rate drops > 15pp from baseline for 30m (signals cache regression)

Non-goals
- No changes to crypto primitives.
- No persistent storage schema changes.
- No new third-party observability vendors.

Implementation notes / constraints
- Keep tag cardinality bounded. Use tenant_id_hash only in restricted/admin surfaces; avoid in general metrics where possible.
- Ensure metrics are emitted in both control-plane and data-plane libraries with consistent naming.
- Coordinate with Security on attribute allowlist for traces.

Acceptance criteria
- Metrics emitted for KMS latency + error codes + cache + breaker state, validated in staging.
- Traces show KMS spans for decrypt/encrypt with correct attributes and no sensitive data.
- Dashboards published and linked in SRE runbook ("KMS dependency degradation").
- Alert rules created in "staging" first; production rules enabled for canary clusters, then expanded.
- Game day uses these dashboards/alerts and produces at least one tuning follow-up.

References
- KMS breaker/retry work: sources/github/redwood/pr_28741.json
- Audit events (complementary, not a replacement for metrics): sources/github/redwood/pr_28805.json
- Dual-read rotation window: sources/github/redwood/pr_28822.json
- Per-tenant health endpoint (ops/debug, separate surface): sources/github/redwood/pr_28910.json
- Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/kms-dependency-degradation-runbook.json
comments: 2026-01-14 (Rafael Mendes): Creating as a dependency for game day. We keep getting "KMS is slow" reports with no breakdown by provider/error code. Need consistent metrics + trace spans before we start intentionally injecting failures.

2026-01-17 (Allison Grant): Drafted metric names + tag policy. Biggest risk is cardinality (tenant_id, key_id, model_route). Proposal: keep tenant dimensions out of default metrics; use a separate admin-only per-tenant summary derived from logs/metrics pipeline (tenant_id hashed) and only enabled for staging + selected canaries initially.

2026-01-22 (Sean Gallagher): Please include breaker state + short-circuit rejections as first-class metrics. During the last brownout we couldn’t tell whether failures were from KMS or from our breaker doing its job. Also want a single dashboard section that answers: "Is this a dependency outage or our config?"

2026-01-28 (Kevin Osei): Tracing attribute allowlist needs to avoid key IDs and tenant IDs. key_alias is okay only if it’s from our config and sanitized (no customer account numbers embedded). Also confirm we’re not logging error messages from provider SDKs verbatim if they contain ARNs/paths.

2026-02-03 (Allison Grant): Implementing data-plane metrics wrapper around the KMS client used by runtime. For Azure/GCP providers, aligning error code taxonomy to common buckets (timeout/throttle/access_denied/key_disabled/not_found/invalid_ciphertext/internal/unknown) so dashboards work cross-provider.

2026-02-09 (Emily Zhao): Heads-up: cache hit rate can look "bad" during rotation dual-read window since we may consult both new and old key metadata. Suggest adding a metric label rotation_mode (normal|dual_read) or at least annotate the dashboard with a rollout marker so oncall doesn’t chase a false regression.

2026-02-12 (Allison Grant): Added initial dashboards in staging. Seeing p99 decrypt latency spikes correlate with AWS KMS throttling in us-east-1 when load tests run with chaos injection. Need to tune default alert threshold to avoid paging on short throttle bursts; propose paging only if decrypt error budget burn > X for 10m.

2026-02-18 (Olga Petrov): For evidence, we need screenshots/exports showing (1) audit events exist (covered by ENG-??/PR 28805) and (2) operational monitoring exists with defined alert thresholds. Please make sure dashboards/alerts are referenced from the control mapping doc in Confluence once stable.

2026-02-21 (Allison Grant): Next steps: wire circuit breaker state metric from PR 28741 into dashboards; add trace span attribute scrubber; create canary-only production alerts (two clusters) and document in runbook. Blocking item: need final sign-off on which metrics are allowed to include tenant_id_hash (Security + SRE).
